definition_zh: 阴天的；多云的；愁云惨淡的；收边的；阴天
definition_en: covered with a continuous layer of grey cloud that hides the sun
core_image: 一块整年的灰毯子从天上铺下来，把太阳盖住
scene: 出门前你抬头看天，只见厚厚一层灰云压着屋顶。The sky was completely overcast before the storm began.
sceneCN: 这里 overcast 是「阴天的」（第 1 个义项：天空被整片灰云盖住）；句意：暴风雨来临前，天空完全阴了下来。

pos.zh: 阴天的；多云的；愁云惨淡的
（用针线）锁边；覆盖
阴天；云层

derivatives.zh: overcast 加名词后缀构成，指布边的锁缝工艺
较少见的旧式拼法，意为「被覆盖的；阴沉的」
同类反义联想词，指低而厚的底层云幕

senses.title: Sky covered by grey cloud
senses.definition: having the sky filled with a flat grey layer of cloud so that the sun cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 天空被整片灰色云层覆盖、看不到太阳的状态
senses.example: It looks overcast, so take an umbrella.
senses.exampleCN: 天看起来很阴，带把伞吧。
senses.why: The prefix over- means across or above, and cast means thrown, so the clouds have been thrown across the whole sky.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「在上方、覆盖过去」，cast 表示「投、抛」，所以阴天就是云被整片投盖在天空上。

senses.title: Gloomy in mood
senses.definition: sad, serious, or threatening in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 神情或气氛显得悲伤、严肃或有威胁感
senses.example: His overcast expression warned us not to ask.
senses.exampleCN: 他阴沉的脸色提醒我们别再问了。
senses.why: A sky that is covered by cloud feels heavy, so the word extends to faces and moods that carry the same weight.
senses.whyCN: 被云盖住的天空使人觉得沉重，于是这个词也延伸到同样沉重的脸色与心情。

senses.title: To sew with a whip stitch
senses.definition: to sew over the raw edge of cloth with long loose stitches so that it cannot unravel
senses.definitionCN: 用长而松的针脚把布的毛边缝住，防止脱线
senses.example: She overcast the edge of the blanket by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手工给毛毯的边缘锁了边。
senses.why: The older verb sense is to cover something by throwing stitches over its edge, the same covering image as the clouds.
senses.whyCN: 较早的动词义是把针脚一圈圈抛盖到布的边缘上，与云层覆盖天空是同一幅覆盖画面。

senses.title: A continuing cloud cover
senses.definition: the state or amount of cloud that continuously covers the sky
senses.definitionCN: 持续覆盖天空的云量或阴天状态
senses.example: Weather reports gave the morning as overcast.
senses.exampleCN: 天气预报把早晨定为阴天。
senses.why: The adjective is often used as a noun label for the whole cloud cover in a weather report.
senses.whyCN: 天气预报常把这个形容词当作名词标签，指整个云层覆盖的状态。

intro.en: Overcast joins over-, meaning across or above, and cast, meaning to throw, so literally it means thrown over.
intro.cn: overcast 由 over-（在上方、覆盖过去）与 cast（投、抛）合成，字面意思是「被抛盖在上面」。

items.en: Cast means to throw, and over means above.
items.cn: 古英语 cast 意为投掷，over 意为在上方。

items.en: The verb spells as overwasten in early forms of the word.
items.cn: 早期书面形式记作 overwasten，是本词的动词形态。

items.en: To overcast means to cover something completely, especially the sky.
items.cn: overcast 表示把某物完全覆盖，尤指天空。

items.en: Sewing makes overcasting a name for a whip stitch on cloth edges.
items.cn: 缝纫领域中，overcast 成为布料锁边针脚的名字。

items.en: The adjective settles into weather talk for a fully clouded sky.
items.cn: 这个形容词固定用于天气描述，指完全被云覆盖的天空。

items.en: Modern use adds the mood sense of a gloomy face or tone.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了形容脸色或语气阴郁的义项。

note.en: Overcast shares the over- family with overcome and overlook, and sits near cloudy, gloomy, and dull in weather talk.
note.cn: overcast 与 overcome、overlook 同属 over- 前缀家族，在天气话题中与 cloudy、gloomy、dull 相邻。

entries.definition: to succeed in dealing with a problem
entries.definitionCN: 克服；战胜

entries.definition: to fail to notice something
entries.definitionCN: 忽略；未注意到

entries.definition: a person rejected by society
entries.definitionCN: 被社会排斥的人；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: having many clouds but still some light
entries.definitionCN: 多云的；云量不等

entries.definition: dark and sad, both in weather and mood
entries.definitionCN: 阴沉沉的；也指忧郁的

entries.definition: not bright, used of grey weather
entries.definitionCN: 昏暗的；不明亮的

normalIntro.en: Overcast is over plus cast: a grey sheet is thrown over the sky.
normalIntro.cn: overcast 就是 over 加 cast：一整张灰布被抛盖在天空上。

normal.en: Cast means to throw, so overcast means thrown over.
normal.cn: cast 意为投掷，所以 overcast 就是被抛盖上去。

normal.en: An overcast sky is a full grey ceiling with no sun.
normal.cn: overcast sky 是整片灰色的天花板，看不见太阳。

normal.en: Cloudy still shows patches of light, overcast hides the sun completely.
normal.cn: cloudy 还露出一块块光，overcast 则把太阳完全遮住。

normal.en: The sewing sense keeps the same image: stitches cover the cloth edge.
normal.cn: 缝纫义保留同一幅画面：针脚把布的边缘盖住。

normal.en: Compare overview and overlook, which also take the over- prefix.
normal.cn: 对比 overview 与 overlook，它们同样带 over- 前缀。

abstract.en: Picture a giant grey blanket pulled slowly across the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一整条巨大的灰毯子被慢慢拉过来，盖在太阳上。

abstract.en: See a person whose face sits under heavy dark clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人脸上压着厚厚的乌云。

abstract.en: Think of long loose threads thrown over a cloth edge, one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一根根长线被抛过布边，一圈圈锁住毛边。

examples.en: The forecast warns of an overcast afternoon with light rain.
examples.cn: 天气预报说下午阴沉，有小雨。

examples.en: Each overcast morning made the whole class feel sleepy.
examples.cn: 每个阴沉的早晨都让全班昏昏欲睡。

examples.en: When the clouds thin, they become cloudy rather than overcast.
examples.cn: 云层变薄时，天气就从阴沉变成多云了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃卡斯特」——欧沃（over）把卡斯特（cast）的灰布抛过天空，天就阴了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 cast（投、抛）+ over（在上方、越过）→ overcast，核心义「被抛盖在整个上方」，故指云层全覆盖的阴沉天空，再引申为脸色阴沉。

sensesIntro.en: Overcast moves from a sky covered by cloud, to a face or mood that feels the same way, to stitches that cover a cloth edge, and finally to a weather report noun.
sensesIntro.cn: overcast 从被云盖住的天空，过渡到同样沉重的脸色与心情，再到盖住布边的锁边针脚，最后成为天气预报里的名词说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey sheet thrown over the sky, hiding the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块灰毯被抛盖在天空上，把太阳遮住。

branches.en: Full cloud cover is the main weather sense.
branches.cn: 云层全覆盖是最主要的天气义项。

branches.en: A covered sky becomes a metaphor for a gloomy face.
branches.cn: 被盖住的天空成了阴沉脸色的隐喻。

branches.en: The sewing verb keeps the same covering picture on cloth.
branches.cn: 缝纫动词把同样的覆盖画面用到了布上。

branches.en: The weather adjective and the weather noun name the same sky.
branches.cn: 天气形容词与阴天名词说的是同一片天空。

branches.en: Both senses share the heavy feeling of being covered.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享被覆盖的沉重感。

intro.en: Overcast is built from the prefix over- and the verb cast, and it stays close to the over- family in modern English.
intro.cn: overcast 由前缀 over- 与动词 cast 构成，在现代英语中仍与 over- 词族关系紧密。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic rather than Latin, so there are no Latin root words for this entry.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，因此本词没有拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix over- adds an above or across meaning.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 增添「在上方、越过」的含义。

items.example: Cast carries the throw image.
items.exampleCN: cast 带来「抛掷」的意象。

items.example: Overcast describes the sky.
items.exampleCN: overcast 描述天空的状态。

items.example: The noun names the weather state.
items.exampleCN: 名词形式指天气状态。

items.example: Overcasting names the sewing stitch.
items.exampleCN: overcasting 指锁边针脚。

items.example: Overcome shares the over- prefix.
items.exampleCN: overcome 共享 over- 前缀。

items.example: Overlook is another over- word.
items.exampleCN: overlook 是另一个 over- 词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms overcasting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overcasting。

items.example: Outcast looks alike but has a different root.
items.exampleCN: outcast 拼写相近，但词源不同。

definition_zh: 大衣；外套；厚外套；（油漆等）表层
definition_en: a long warm coat worn over other clothes in cold weather
core_image: 一件厚实的深色长外套套在西装外面，挡风挡雪
scene: 冬天出门，你先把围巾围好，再套上一件厚实的大衣。He put on a heavy overcoat before walking into the snow.
sceneCN: 这里 overcoat 是「大衣」（第 1 个义项：穿在其他衣服外面的保暖长外套）；句意：他走进雪地前穿上了厚重的厚大衣。

pos.zh: 大衣；外套；厚外套

derivatives.zh: overcoat 减掉前缀 over- 后的基础词，泛指外套
overcoat 加 -less 后缀构成，义为「没穿大衣的」
近义复合词，指轻便的外层大衣或漆面表层

senses.title: A long coat over other clothes
senses.definition: a long, heavy coat worn outdoors over other clothes to keep warm
senses.definitionCN: 在户外穿在其他衣服外面、用来保暖的长款厚外套
senses.example: He wore a dark overcoat and a scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着一件深色大衣，围着围巾。
senses.why: Over- means on top of, and coat is the garment, so an overcoat is literally the coat worn over the coat.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示「在上面」，coat 表示外套，所以 overcoat 字面就是「套在外套外面的那件外套」。

senses.title: Formal winter outerwear
senses.definition: a smart tailored coat forming the outer layer of a formal winter outfit
senses.definitionCN: 剪裁考究、构成正式冬装最外层的长外套
senses.example: The guests left their overcoats at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 宾客们把大衣留在门口。
senses.why: Because it covers the formal suit, the overcoat became a marker of a tidy winter outfit for work and events.
senses.whyCN: 因为它罩在正式西装外，大衣就成了工作和正式场合里整洁冬装的一部分。

senses.title: Outer coating layer
senses.definition: an outer layer of paint or material applied over a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面之上的漆层或材料外层
senses.example: Apply the overcoat once the base layer is dry.
senses.exampleCN: 底层干了以后再涂表层漆。
senses.why: The technical sense borrows the same over- image and puts an extra layer over the base surface.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法借用同一幅覆盖画面，在底面上再盖一层。

intro.en: Overcoat is a simple English compound of over-, meaning above, and coat, meaning an outer garment.
intro.cn: overcoat 是纯粹的英语复合词，由 over-（在上方）与 coat（外衣）构成。

items.en: Cote names a coarse outer tunic or habit.
items.cn: 古法语 cote 指粗糙的外层束腰外衣或长袍。

items.en: Cote enters English as coat, the outer garment.
items.cn: cote 以 coat 的形式进入英语，指外层衣物。

items.en: Coat extends to any outer covering, including armed jackets.
items.cn: coat 扩展为泛指外层衣物，包括带铠甲的短上衣。

items.en: Overcoat appears for a heavy coat worn over normal clothing.
items.cn: overcoat 出现，指穿在平常衣服外面的厚外套。

items.en: Tailored overcoats become standard winter wear for city work.
items.cn: 剪裁考究的大衣成为城市冬季上班的标准装束。

items.en: Modern use adds a technical sense for outer paint layers.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表层涂料的专业义项。

note.en: Overcoat is a compound in the over- family and sits with generic coat words and winter clothing terms.
note.cn: overcoat 属于 over- 词族，与通用的外套词和冬季衣物词相邻。

entries.definition: an outer garment worn for warmth
entries.definitionCN: 外套；外衣

entries.definition: a sleeveless garment worn under a jacket
entries.definitionCN: 马甲；背心

entries.definition: a light outer coat or an outer paint layer
entries.definitionCN: 轻便的大衣；漆面表层

entries.definition: any general outer garment
entries.definitionCN: 泛指各类外套

entries.definition: a loose sleeveless outer garment
entries.definitionCN: 斗篷；披风

entries.definition: a short coat that ends at the hips
entries.definitionCN: 夹克；短外套

normalIntro.en: Overcoat is over plus coat: the coat you put over the coat.
normalIntro.cn: overcoat 就是 over 加 coat：穿在外套外面的那件外套。

normal.en: Over- means on top, so an overcoat goes over your shirt and suit.
normal.cn: over- 表示在上面，所以大衣要罩在衬衫和西装外面。

normal.en: A plain coat can be short, an overcoat is long and heavy.
normal.cn: 普通的 coat 可长可短，overcoat 则长而厚实。

normal.en: The plural is overcoats, simply adding s.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s，写成 overcoats。

normal.en: In paint work, the overcoat is the layer over the base coat.
normal.cn: 在刷漆时，overcoat 是涂在底层漆之上的那一层。

normal.en: Compare waistcoat and topcoat for other coat compounds.
normal.cn: 对比 waistcoat 与 topcoat，看看其他 coat 复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a long dark coat swinging open as someone steps out of the cold.
abstract.cn: 想象有人从寒风中走进来，敞开一件深色长大衣。

abstract.en: See a row of formal overcoats hanging in a warm hallway.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖的走廊里挂着一排正式的大衣。

abstract.en: Think of a second brush stroke laid over the first one on a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门上先刷了一道漆，又在其上刷了第二道。

examples.en: She hung her overcoat on the hook by the door.
examples.cn: 她把大衣挂在门边的挂钩上。

examples.en: Two overcoats were left behind on the train.
examples.cn: 火车上落下了两件大衣。

examples.en: A wool overcoat keeps out the wind on a winter walk.
examples.cn: 冬天散步时，一件羊毛大衣能挡风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃扣特」——欧沃（over）一层再扣上衣扣，就是大衣；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: over（古英语，意为在上方）+ coat（源自法语 cote，指外层衣物）→ overcoat，核心义「罩在其他衣服外面的外套」。

sensesIntro.en: Overcoat starts as the warm coat worn over everything else, then names the formal winter outer layer, and finally extends to an outer layer of paint.
sensesIntro.cn: overcoat 先指罩在所有衣物外面的保暖外套，再指正式场合的冬装最外层，最后延伸到油漆等表面之上的涂层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy long coat slipped over a suit to block the cold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件厚长大衣套在西装外面挡住寒风。

branches.en: The warm long coat is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 保暖的长外套是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Wearing it over a suit gives the formal sense.
branches.cn: 罩在西装外穿着带来正式场合的义项。

branches.en: Layers of paint reuse the over- image for surfaces.
branches.cn: 油漆分层复用了 over- 的覆盖意象。

branches.en: Both senses put one layer over another layer.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是在一层之上再盖一层。

branches.en: The same garment serves warmth and formal dress.
branches.cn: 同一件外套既保暖又服务于正式着装。

intro.en: Overcoat combines the prefix over- with the noun coat, and it stays near other over- compounds.
intro.cn: overcoat 由前缀 over- 与名词 coat 组合而成，与其他 over- 复合词关系紧密。

latinIntro.en: The base coat comes through French from Latin cottus, a coarse outer garment.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 coat 经法语来自拉丁语 cottus，指粗糙的外层衣物。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标示最外层。

items.example: Coat is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: coat 是复合词的词干。

items.example: Overcoat names the warm outer coat.
items.exampleCN: overcoat 指保暖的长外套。

items.example: The plural adds s to the compound.
items.exampleCN: 复数在词尾加 s。

items.example: The suffix -less forms overcoatless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 overcoatless。

items.example: Topcoat is a close compound kin.
items.exampleCN: topcoat 是近亲复合词。

items.example: Raincoat shares the coat pattern.
items.exampleCN: raincoat 共享 coat 复合模式。

items.example: Overall shows another over- use.
items.exampleCN: overall 展示了 over- 的另一用法。

items.meaning: a protective shoe worn over another
items.example: Overshoe follows the same over- pattern.
items.exampleCN: overshoe 遵循同样的 over- 构词模式。

definition_en: to put too many people or things into one place
core_image: 一辆小巴里人贴着人，连门口都站满了人
scene: 早高峰的地铁车厢里，人挤得背包都打不开。Tourists overcrowd the small beach every summer.
sceneCN: 这里 overcrowd 是「使过度拥挤」（第 1 个义项：把过多的人和物塞进一处）；句意：每到夏天，游客就把这片小海滩挤得满满当当。

pos.zh: 使过度拥挤；塞满；挤满
变得过分拥挤；涌满

derivatives.zh: overcrowd 加 -ed 后缀构成，义为「过度拥挤的」
overcrowd 加 -ing 后缀构成的名词，指拥挤状况
去掉前缀 over- 后的基础词，指人群

senses.title: To fill a place with too many people
senses.definition: to put so many people into a place that it is hard to move or breathe
senses.definitionCN: 把过多的人塞进一个地方，以至于难以走动或呼吸
senses.example: Officials should not overcrowd the shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们不该让避难所过度拥挤。
senses.why: Over- means too much, and crowd means to fill with a crowd, so overcrowd is to add a crowd on top of a crowd.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示过度，crowd 表示把人塞成一群，所以 overcrowd 就是在人群之上再塞进人群。

senses.title: To be too full of things
senses.definition: to pack a place or space so full of objects that it is uncomfortable or unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 把一个地方或空间塞满物品，以至于不舒适或不安全
senses.example: Boxes overcrowd the small office.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子把这个小办公室堆满了。
senses.why: The object can be goods as well as people, because the core idea is simply exceeding the safe capacity.
senses.whyCN: 被塞满的对象也可以是货物，因为核心意思只是超过了安全的容量。

senses.title: To press in and take over
senses.definition: to flock into a place in such numbers that locals are pushed out
senses.definitionCN: 成群涌入某地，以致当地人的生活空间被挤占
senses.example: Cruise ships overcrowd the old harbour each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每到春天，游轮就把这个老港口挤得水泄不通。
senses.why: The verb can be used of a flock of visitors whose sheer numbers squeeze out those already there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指一大群外来者，用数量把原本在那里的人挤出去。

intro.en: Overcrowd is formed from over-, meaning too much, and the verb crowd, which comes from the noun crowd, a press of people.
intro.cn: overcrowd 由 over-（过度）与动词 crowd 构成，而 crowd 又来自名词 crowd，指挤在一起的一群人。

items.en: Crudan means to press, push, or crowd together.
items.cn: 古英语 crudan 意为挤、推、拥挤在一起。

items.en: Crouden takes the press together sense into English.
items.cn: crouden 把「挤在一起」的含义带入英语。

items.en: Crowd appears as a noun for a dense mass of people.
items.cn: crowd 作为名词出现，指密密麻麻的一群人。

items.en: Overcrowd forms by adding over- in the sense of too much.
items.cn: 加上表示「过度」的 over-，构成 overcrowd。

items.en: Industrial cities give the word a public health and housing meaning.
items.cn: 工业城市让这个词获得了公共卫生与住房方面的含义。

items.en: Modern use covers transport, prisons, schools, hospitals, and tourism.
items.cn: 现代英语把用法扩展到交通、监狱、学校、医院与旅游业。

note.en: Overcrowd is an over- verb built on crowd, and it sits with words for packing and jamming a space.
note.cn: overcrowd 是以 crowd 为基础构成的 over- 动词，与表示塞满、堵塞的词相邻。

entries.definition: to come together in large numbers
entries.definitionCN: 群集；挤在一起

entries.definition: holding too many people or things
entries.definitionCN: 过度拥挤的

entries.definition: the state of being too full
entries.definitionCN: 拥挤状况；超员

entries.definition: to fill a space tightly
entries.definitionCN: 塞满；装满

entries.definition: to block or squeeze into a space
entries.definitionCN: 堵塞；塞入

entries.definition: to push things tightly into a container
entries.definitionCN: 塞进；填塞

normalIntro.en: Overcrowd is over plus crowd: a crowd stacked on top of another crowd.
normalIntro.cn: overcrowd 就是 over 加 crowd：一群人在另一群人身上又叠了一层。

normal.en: Over- means too much, so to overcrowd is to crowd too much.
normal.cn: over- 表示过度，所以 overcrowd 就是挤得太过。

normal.en: An overcrowded bus has no room to stand.
normal.cn: overcrowded bus 是连站都站不下的公交。

normal.en: The adjective adds -ed, the noun adds -ing.
normal.cn: 形容词形式加 -ed，名词形式加 -ing。

normal.en: Prisons and hospitals use this word for unsafe numbers.
normal.cn: 监狱和医院用这个词表示不安全的超员数量。

normal.en: Compare crowd, which is neutral, with overcrowd, which is negative.
normal.cn: 对比 crowd 是中性的，overcrowd 则带贬义。

abstract.en: Picture a small room where every seat is taken and people stand at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小屋子座位全满，门口还站着一排人。

abstract.en: See a shelf with so many boxes that the top one nearly falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一个架子塞满箱子，最上面的那个快掉下来了。

abstract.en: Think of a road of slow buses that push out the local shoppers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路上缓慢移动的观光车，把本地的购物者挤到一旁。

examples.en: Large hotels could overcrowd the quiet coastal village.
examples.cn: 大型酒店可能会让这个安静的沿海村庄变得过于拥挤。

examples.en: Trains overcrowd quickly during the evening rush.
examples.cn: 晚高峰时段火车很快就挤满了人。

examples.en: The old prison was badly overcrowded last winter.
examples.cn: 去年冬天，那座旧监狱严重超员拥挤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃客绕得」——欧沃（over）让人客绕得来都走不动，就是过度拥挤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: over（过度、在上方）+ crowd（源自中古英语 crouden，挤在一起、压迫）→ overcrowd，核心义「挤到超出容量」。

sensesIntro.en: Overcrowd starts with too many people and too little room, widens to too many objects in a space, and then covers a flood of visitors squeezing out the locals.
sensesIntro.cn: overcrowd 先指人多地方小，扩展到物品把空间塞满，再指大批外来者把原本的人挤出去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bus with a wall of people pressing against the doors.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆挤到门口贴满人的公共汽车。

branches.en: Too many people is the main sense.
branches.cn: 人太多是最主要的义项。

branches.en: Too many objects is the extension to goods.
branches.cn: 物品太多是对货物场景的延伸。

branches.en: Too many visitors pushing locals aside is the social sense.
branches.cn: 外来者太多、挤占本地人空间是社会层面的义项。

branches.en: Both senses break the safe capacity of a space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都突破了空间的安全容量。

branches.en: Both senses begin with numbers that overwhelm the place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是从压倒一切的数量开始。

intro.en: Overcrowd combines the prefix over- with the verb crowd, and its -ed and -ing forms carry most of its everyday use.
intro.cn: overcrowd 由前缀 over- 与动词 crowd 组合而成，日常使用中大多是它的 -ed 与 -ing 形式。

latinIntro.en: Crowd is Germanic in origin and has no Latin root words, so the Latin relatives are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: crowd 源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根同源词，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

items.example: The prefix over- marks excess.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标示过度。

items.meaning: to come together in large numbers
items.example: Crowd is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: crowd 是基础动词。

items.meaning: to fill with too many people
items.example: Overcrowd adds excess to crowd.
items.exampleCN: overcrowd 在 crowd 上加了「过度」。

items.example: The third person form adds s.
items.exampleCN: 三单形式加 s。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms overcrowded.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 overcrowded。

items.meaningCN: 构成名词或现在分词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms overcrowding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overcrowding。

items.example: Crowded is the neutral adjective.
items.exampleCN: crowded 是中性的形容词。

items.example: Overcrowded is the common adjective form.
items.exampleCN: overcrowded 是常用的形容词形式。

items.meaning: too many people in an area
items.example: Overpopulation is a related over- noun.
items.exampleCN: overpopulation 是相关的 over- 名词。

items.meaning: to put too much weight on
items.example: Overload shows the same excess pattern.
items.exampleCN: overload 展示同样的「过度」构词模式。

definition_en: an amount that a bank lets you take out beyond the money in your account, or the right to do this
core_image: 账本的余额线被一支笔向下划过，画出一条低于零的红色缺口
scene: 月租自动扣款那天账上钱不够，银行替她垫付，账面变成了负数。The rent went out by direct debit and left her with an overdraft of thirty pounds at the bank.
sceneCN: 这里 overdraft 是「透支额」（第 1 个义项：银行允许你取出超过余额的钱）；句意：月租自动扣款那天账上钱不够，银行替她垫付，账面变成了负数。

pos.zh: 透支；透支额；透支款项
透支（账户）

collocations.zh: 透支额度（银行批准的透支便利）
事先约定好的透支额度

derivatives.zh: overdraw 的过去式，基础动词加前缀 over- 表示「取过头」，义为「透支取出；超额提取」
overdraw 的过去分词转为形容词，义为「已透支的；余额为负的」
over-（超过）+ draw（取出），由动作名词逆构出的动词，义为「透支账户」
由 overdraft 加分词后缀 -ing 转化为抽象名词，义为「透支行为；透支现象」

senses.title: The extra money the bank lets you use
senses.titleCN: 透支额；可供透支的款项
senses.definition: an amount that a bank allows a customer to withdraw beyond the money held in the account
senses.definitionCN: 银行允许客户取出、超出其账户余额的那部分钱
senses.example: The bank agreed to raise his overdraft to two thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 银行同意把他的透支额提高到两千英镑。
senses.why: The prefix over- means beyond and draft once meant an amount drawn or taken, so an overdraft is money drawn beyond what is there.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「超过」，draft 早期指「提取的款项」，所以透支额就是取到了余额之外的那部分钱。

senses.title: A negative balance
senses.titleCN: 账户余额为负；账面欠款
senses.definition: the debt left in an account when more money has been taken out than was paid in
senses.definitionCN: 账户支出多于存入后留下的欠款状态或欠款数
senses.example: He was shocked to see an overdraft of ninety pounds on his statement.
senses.exampleCN: 看到对账单上有九十英镑的负余额，他吃了一惊。
senses.why: The amount drawn beyond the balance becomes a debt recorded in the account itself, which is why the same noun names the negative figure.
senses.whyCN: 取到余额之外的金额会以欠款形式记在账户里，所以这个名词也指账面上那个负数。

senses.title: The right to overdraw
senses.definition: an agreement under which a bank lets a customer overdraw instead of refusing payment
senses.definitionCN: 银行与客户之间允许超额支取、而不是拒绝付款的约定
senses.example: She signed up for an arranged overdraft when she opened the current account.
senses.exampleCN: 开立活期账户时，她一并申请了约好的透支安排。
senses.why: A bank does not simply allow unlimited overdrawing, so the word also names the agreed permission that makes overdrawing possible.
senses.whyCN: 银行不会无条件允许无限透支，于是这个词也指那项使透支得以发生的约定权限。

senses.title: The charge for overdrawing
senses.definition: the fee or interest that a bank charges for letting an account go below zero
senses.definitionCN: 银行因允许账户余额变为负数而收取的手续费或利息
senses.example: A daily overdraft charge quickly ate into her small savings.
senses.exampleCN: 按日计算的透支费很快就吃掉了她微薄的存款。
senses.why: Once the arrangement exists, the bank prices it, so overdraft in financial writing often means the cost of borrowing in this way.
senses.whyCN: 安排一旦存在，银行就会为其定价，因此在财经文本中 overdraft 常指这种借钱的成本。

senses.title: To draw beyond the limit
senses.definition: to take more money from an account than it holds
senses.definitionCN: 从账户中取出超过其存款金额的钱
senses.example: Companies may overdraft their accounts while waiting for payments.
senses.exampleCN: 公司等待回款期间可能会透支账户。
senses.why: English often reverses a compound noun back into a verb, so the action hidden in draft reappears in the simple sense to overdraw.
senses.whyCN: 英语常从复合名词逆构出动词，于是 draft 里隐含的「支取」动作重新出现，形成「透支取出」的意思。

intro.en: Overdraft joins over, meaning beyond, to draft, whose sense of drawing or taking out of a fund dates from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: overdraft 由 over（超出）加上 draft 构成，而 draft 表示「支取、开票取款」的用法出现在十九世纪。

items.en: Over and draft, Old English ofer and draeht, both go back to Germanic material; neither word is borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: over 与 draft（古英语 ofer 与 draeht）都回溯到日耳曼语，两词均非借自拉丁语。

items.en: Draft first meant something drawn or pulled, and later a written order for money.
items.cn: draft 最初指被拉或拖出的东西，后来指支取钱的书面命令。

items.en: A draft names a bill of exchange, a document asking one party to pay another.
items.cn: draft 指汇票，即要求一方付款给另一方的凭据。

items.en: Overdraft appears in British banking as the amount drawn over the credit balance.
items.cn: overdraft 在十九世纪的英国银行界出现，指超出存款余额而支取的款项。

items.en: Banks formalise arranged overdrafts for current accounts, and the word becomes everyday.
items.cn: 二十世纪银行把透支安排规范化为活期账户的一部分，这个词进入日常用语。

items.en: Digital banking lets customers see their overdraft limit on screen.
items.cn: 数字银行让客户在屏幕上直接看到自己的透支额度。

note.en: Overdraft is built from over plus a banking draft, so it belongs with over- words and with everyday account terms.
note.cn: overdraft 由 over 与银行用语的 draft 构成，因此既与 over- 词族相邻，也处在账户术语的义场中。

entries.definition: a written order for payment, or a rough version
entries.definitionCN: 汇票；草稿；这是构成复合词的核心部件

entries.definition: to take out more money than an account holds
entries.definitionCN: 透支账户

entries.definition: not paid or done by the expected time
entries.definitionCN: 过期的；逾期未付的；与 overdraft 共用前缀 over-，但后接词根不同

entries.definition: the act of drawing money beyond the balance
entries.definitionCN: 支取超出余额的行为

entries.definition: money borrowed and repaid over time
entries.definitionCN: 贷款；与透支不同，通常有明确期限

entries.definition: money that is owed
entries.definitionCN: 债务；余额为负时形成的东西

normalIntro.en: Overdraft is a picture of taking out more than is inside: over plus draft, the drawn amount.
normalIntro.cn: overdraft 就是「取出的多于里面有的」：over 表示超过，draft 表示被支取的款项。

normal.en: Over- means too much, as in overeat and oversleep.
normal.cn: 前缀 over- 表示过度，就像 overeat（吃太多）和 oversleep（睡过头）。

normal.en: A bank draft is an order for money, so draft carries the idea of paying out.
normal.cn: bank draft 是支取令，可见 draft 带着「付出去」的意思。

normal.en: An arranged overdraft is agreed in advance, an unauthorised one is not.
normal.cn: arranged overdraft 是事先约好的，unauthorised overdraft 则是未经许可的。

normal.en: To be overdrawn is to be in the red, so the adjective ends in -n like drawn.
normal.cn: overdrawn 就是「赤字」，这个形容词与 drawn 同尾。

normal.en: Compare overdraft with overdue: one is about money taken, the other about time passed.
normal.cn: 对比 overdue：一个讲钱取多了，一个讲时间过了。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk sliding a ruler down past the zero line.
abstract.cn: 想象一位银行职员把尺子一路滑到零线以下。

abstract.en: Imagine a wallet that opens wider than the money inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包张开得比里面的钱还大。

abstract.en: Think of a safety rope long enough for you to reach beyond the cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条足够长的安全绳，让你能探到悬崖边的外面。

examples.en: Most students avoid an overdraft by working part time.
examples.cn: 大多数学生靠做兼职避免透支。

examples.en: The shop paid her wages late, so she ran into an overdraft.
examples.cn: 商店晚发了她的工资，于是她陷入了透支。

examples.en: He paid off his overdraft as soon as the bonus arrived.
examples.cn: 奖金一到手，他就还清了透支款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧弗-抓夫特」听起来像「over 抓」，钱被「超额抓」出了账户，就是透支；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ofer（在上、超过）+ 中古英语 draught（被拉出的东西、支取的钱）→ 十九世纪银行用语 overdraft（超出余额支取的款项）→ 现代义「透支；透支额」。

sensesIntro.en: Overdraft starts from money drawn beyond the balance, then names the negative balance, the agreed permission, its price, and finally the action itself.
sensesIntro.cn: overdraft 从「取到余额之外的款项」出发，进而指负余额、约定权限、透支费用，最后回到「透支」这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an amount drawn just beyond the zero line of an account.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔被取到账户零线之外的款子。

branches.en: The extra money available beyond the balance is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 超出余额可用的那笔钱是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Once that money is spent, the account shows a negative figure.
branches.cn: 这笔钱一旦花出，账户上就出现负数。

branches.en: The bank states how far you may overdraw by agreement.
branches.cn: 银行用约定说明你可以透支到何种程度。

branches.en: Borrowing beyond the balance is priced as a fee or interest.
branches.cn: 超出余额借款要按手续费或利息计价。

branches.en: The noun names the money, the verb names the act of taking it.
branches.cn: 名词指那笔钱，动词指取出它的动作。

intro.en: Overdraft is a native Germanic compound of over and draft, and English compounds it further into overdraw, overdrawn, and overdrafting.
intro.cn: overdraft 是由 over 与 draft 构成的日耳曼语系复合词，英语又围绕它造出 overdraw、overdrawn 与 overdrafting。

latinIntro.en: Neither over nor draft comes from Latin, so this word has no Latin family; its neighbours are Germanic over- compounds such as overdue and overestimate.
latinIntro.cn: over 与 draft 都不来自拉丁语，这个词没有拉丁同族；它的邻居是 overdue、overestimate 这类日耳曼语 over- 复合词。

items.example: The prefix over- marks the excess in overdraft.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标出透支中的「超出」。

items.meaning: a drawing out of money; a rough version
items.example: Draft supplies the money-drawing part of the word.
items.exampleCN: draft 提供这个词「支取钱款」的部分。

items.example: Overdraft is the compound itself.
items.exampleCN: overdraft 就是这个词本身。

items.meaning: to take out more than is held
items.example: Overdraw puts the action back into a verb.
items.exampleCN: overdraw 把动作重新放回动词里。

items.example: Drawn becomes overdrawn in the participle.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式把 drawn 变成 overdrawn。

items.meaning: forming nouns for actions or processes
items.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或过程的名词
items.example: The suffix -ing forms overdrafting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overdrafting。

items.example: Overdrafts keeps the plural ending.
items.exampleCN: overdrafts 保留复数词尾。

items.example: Overdue shares the prefix but not the draft.
items.exampleCN: overdue 共用前缀，但不含 draft。

items.meaning: to judge as larger than it is
items.example: Overestimate shows the same over- pattern.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 展示了同样的 over- 结构模式。

definition_zh: 过期的；逾期的；过期未付的；迟到的；早该发生的
definition_en: not paid or done by the time it was expected, or happening later than it should have
core_image: 日历上的红圈已经翻过去好几页，旁边的那一行账目仍空着没划掉
scene: 图书馆借的书早过了还书日期，系统自动发来提醒。The library books were overdue by nine days, so the system sent her a reminder.
sceneCN: 这里 overdue 是「过期的」（第 1 个义项：超过了规定的期限而尚未完成）；句意：图书馆借的书早过了还书日期，系统自动发来提醒。

pos.zh: 过期的；逾期的；迟到的；早该发生的

collocations.zh: 早就该有的；姗姗来迟的

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 over- 的基础形容词，义为「到期的；应付的」
前缀 un-（相反）+ due，义为「过分的；不应有的」，与 overdue 的 over- 方向相反
due 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「按时地；适当地」
overdue 加名词后缀 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「逾期状态」

senses.title: Past its due date
senses.definition: not done, paid, or returned by the date set for it
senses.definitionCN: 未在规定的日期完成、支付或归还
senses.example: Your electricity bill is overdue and interest will be added.
senses.exampleCN: 你的电费已经逾期，将会加收利息。
senses.why: Over- means beyond and due means owed or owed as a date, so anything still unpaid after its date is beyond due.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「超过」，due 表示「应付的、到期的」，因此过了到期日仍未完成的，就是「过了应期」。

senses.title: Approaching the day an important event is expected
senses.definition: having gone past the expected date for a baby to be born
senses.definitionCN: 已经超过预计的出生日期而尚未分娩
senses.example: She is nearly two weeks overdue with her first baby.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀第一个孩子，已经超过预产期快两周了。
senses.why: The expected date works like a due date, so a birth past that date is described with the same beyond-due image.
senses.whyCN: 预产期和到期日是同一类「期限」，所以超过预产期也用同一种「超期」的意象来描写。

senses.title: Long deserved but slow to arrive
senses.titleCN: 早该发生却迟来的；姗姗来迟的
senses.definition: deserved or needed for a long time and finally happening
senses.definitionCN: 很早以前就该拥有或需要，如今才终于发生
senses.example: An apology from the council was long overdue.
senses.exampleCN: 道歉本该早就来自市政委员会，如今才终于出现。
senses.why: The literal overdue date turns figurative: the debt of time has piled up, so the event arrives later than it was owed.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的「过期」转向比喻：时间的「欠款」越积越多，于是这件事来得比应得的更晚。

intro.en: Overdue is simply over plus due, both native Germanic words, and the compound appears in English records from the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: overdue 就是 over 加 due，两个词都来自日耳曼语系，这个复合形式在十七世纪的英语记录中出现。

items.en: Ofer means over or beyond, and due traces back to French deu, from Latin debere, to owe.
items.cn: ofer 意为在上、超过，而 due 可回溯到法语 deu，再到拉丁语 debere（欠）。

items.en: Debere gives debitum, that which is owed, the ancestor of English due and debt.
items.cn: debere 派生 debitum（所欠之物），这是英语 due 与 debt 的祖先。

items.en: Deu, later deù, means owed or expected, and enters English as due.
items.cn: 法语 deu（后写作 deù）意为应支付的、预期的，进入英语成为 due。

items.en: Overdue is first recorded meaning later than what was expected, and quickly spreads to payments and library books.
items.cn: overdue 最早被记录为「比预期晚」，随后很快用于款项支付和图书馆借书。

items.en: Shipping and railway timetables popularise overdue for late arrivals.
items.cn: 十九世纪的航运与铁路时刻表让 overdue 广泛用来说明「晚到」。

items.en: Modern English also uses overdue figuratively for praise and change long deserved.
items.cn: 现代英语也用 overdue 比喻早该得到的称赞与早该发生的改变。

note.en: Overdue sits on the native due (from Latin debere), and its over- prefix links it to other beyond-words.
note.cn: overdue 建立在日耳曼语系的 due（源自拉丁语 debere）之上，其前缀 over- 又把它与其他表示「超过」的词连成一片。

entries.definition: expected or owed at a stated time
entries.definitionCN: 到期的；应付的；去掉 over- 后的基础词

entries.definition: more than is right or reasonable
entries.definitionCN: 过分的；不应有的；与 overdue 方向相反的否定形式

entries.definition: to do too much of something
entries.definitionCN: 做得过分；共用前缀 over-，但词根不同

entries.definition: arriving after the expected time
entries.definitionCN: 迟到的；晚的

entries.definition: failing to pay a debt or do a duty on time
entries.definitionCN: 拖欠的；失职的

entries.definition: coming later than it should
entries.definitionCN: 迟来的；来迟的

normalIntro.en: Overdue is a deadline crossed: over the due line, the thing still has not been done.
normalIntro.cn: overdue 是越过截止线的状态：越过了 due（到期）这条线，事情还没办完。

normal.en: Due means owed or expected, as in rent due on the first.
normal.cn: due 表示应付的、到期的，如租金到期。

normal.en: Adding over- makes it beyond due, that is, past the date.
normal.cn: 加上 over- 就成了「超过应期」，也就是过了日期。

normal.en: Long overdue is praise for something that should have happened years ago.
normal.cn: long overdue 指某件事早该发生，如今才来。

normal.en: Overdue for means it is time a person or thing had something.
normal.cn: overdue for 表示某人或某事物早该进行某项安排了。

normal.en: Compare due and debt: both come from Latin debere, to owe.
normal.cn: 对比 due 与 debt：二者都来自拉丁语 debere（欠）。

abstract.en: Picture a red circle on a calendar with several pages already turned.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上画着红圈，而好几页已经被翻过去了。

abstract.en: Imagine a report card stamped with the word late.
abstract.cn: 想象一张成绩单被盖上了「迟到」的章。

abstract.en: See a well-used book still sitting on the desk after its return date.
abstract.cn: 看见那本被翻旧的书还躺在桌上，早已过了还书日期。

examples.en: The payment for the hospital bill is now three weeks overdue.
examples.cn: 这笔医疗账单现在已经逾期三周。

examples.en: His bus was overdue, so he took a taxi.
examples.cn: 他等的公交车迟迟不来，于是改坐出租车。

examples.en: A separate waiting room for patients was long overdue.
examples.cn: 单独的候诊室早就该有了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧弗丢」——东西「over（过了）」期限还「丢」在原地没还，就是逾期；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ofer（超过）+ 拉丁语 debere（欠）→ 法语 deu（应付的）→ 英语 due（到期的）→ 十七世纪英语复合词 overdue（超过应期）。

sensesIntro.en: Overdue first means beyond its due date, then the specific past-due date for a birth, and finally anything long deserved that arrives late.
sensesIntro.cn: overdue 先指超过到期日，再特指超过预产期，最后引申为一切早该到来却姗姗来迟的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deadline line on the calendar already crossed.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上那条截止线已经被越过。

branches.en: Anything unpaid or unreturned after its date is overdue.
branches.cn: 过了日期仍未付、未还的，都属于逾期。

branches.en: An expected birth date works like a due date, and a birth after it is overdue.
branches.cn: 预产期就像一条到期日，越过它而尚未分娩便属于超期。

branches.en: What should have come long ago arrives too late, so the word turns figurative.
branches.cn: 早该出现的事物来得很晚，于是这个词转向比喻义。

branches.en: Both describe a date that has been passed without the event happening.
branches.cn: 两者都描述日期已过而事情尚未发生。

branches.en: The literal unpaid bill and the figurative overdue apology share the same debt of time.
branches.cn: 字面上逾期未付的账单与比喻上迟来的道歉，都欠着同一笔时间债。

intro.en: Overdue is a native Germanic compound, over plus due, a word that itself came through French from Latin debere.
intro.cn: overdue 是日耳曼语系的复合词，由 over 与 due 组成，而 due 本身经法语来自拉丁语 debere。

latinIntro.en: Only due, from Latin debere to owe, carries a Latin history; over is native English, so the Latin family here is small.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 due 带有拉丁渊源（来自拉丁语 debere，意为欠），over 是英语本族词，因此这里的拉丁同族并不算多。

items.example: The prefix over- means beyond in overdue.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 在 overdue 中表示「超过」。

items.meaning: owed or expected at a set time
items.example: Due gives the deadline image.
items.exampleCN: due 提供截止期限的意象。

items.example: Overdue is the whole word.
items.exampleCN: overdue 就是整个词。

items.example: The prefix un- forms undue.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 undue。

items.example: Undue is the negative partner of due.
items.exampleCN: undue 是 due 的否定对应词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms duly from due.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 由 due 构成 duly。

items.example: Overly shares the over- pattern of excess.
items.exampleCN: overly 与 overdue 共享 over- 的「过度」模式。

items.example: Debere is the distant source of due.
items.exampleCN: debere 是 due 的古老源头。

latinEntries.meaning: to owe, to be under obligation
a debt, that which is owed

definition_zh: 高估；估计过高；估得过大；过高估计（名词）
definition_en: to judge a number, value, or ability as larger than it really is, or such an estimate
core_image: 秤盘上那一端被压得太低，因为心里给它加了一块看不见的砝码
scene: 装修师傅按最坏情况算了工时，结果只花了一半时间来开工。The builder estimated two months for the job, but he had overestimated the work.
sceneCN: 这里 overestimate 是「高估」（第 1 个义项：把数量或数值估计得比实际更大）；句意：装修师傅按最坏情况算了工时，结果只花了一半时间来开工。

pos.zh: 高估；估计过高；估得过大
过高的估计；高估的数额

derivatives.zh: overestimate 去词尾 -e 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「高估；估计过高」
换用前缀 under-（不足），义为「低估」，是 overestimate 最直接的反义配对
estimate 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「估计；判断」，是这一词族的抽象名词
过去分词转为形容词，义为「被高估的」

senses.title: To guess a number too high
senses.definition: to judge a number, amount, or value as greater than it actually is
senses.definitionCN: 把数量、金额或数值判断得比实际情况更大
senses.example: Ten thousand people attended, far fewer than the organiser overestimated.
senses.exampleCN: 到场者一万人左右，远少于组织者高估的数字。
senses.why: The prefix over- means more, and estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value, so overestimate is to put too high a value on a number.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「多于」，estimate 来自拉丁语 aestimare（估价），所以高估就是给一个数字标价过高。

senses.title: To regard someone as more capable than they are
senses.definition: to think that a person, group, or thing is stronger or more capable than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人、某群体或某事物比实际更强或更有能力
senses.example: The manager overestimated her team and gave them a task they could not finish.
senses.exampleCN: 经理高估了自己的团队，给了一项他们无法完成的任务。
senses.why: Once the sense shifts from numbers to people, the same extra weight becomes a judgement of ability.
senses.whyCN: 当对象从数字转到人，这份「多出来的分量」就变成了对能力的判断。

senses.title: An estimate that is too high
senses.definition: a figure or judgement that is higher than what is true
senses.definitionCN: 一个高于真实情况的数字或判断
senses.example: The council made a serious overestimate of housing demand.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会对住房需求作出了严重过高的估计。
senses.why: English lets the verb serve as a noun, so the act and its result keep one form, as in a large overestimate.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许动词直接充当名词，因此行为和结果共用一种形式，如 a large overestimate。

intro.en: Overestimate is over plus estimate, and estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value or appraise; the compound is recorded in English from the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: overestimate 是 over 加 estimate，而 estimate 来自拉丁语 aestimare（估计、估价）；这个复合词在十八世纪的英语中开始被记录。

items.en: Aestimare means to value, appraise, or reckon something worth a certain amount.
items.cn: aestimare 意为估价、评值或核算某物值多少。

items.en: Aestimatio and the participle aestimatus supply the forms that French and English later borrow.
items.cn: aestimatio 与分词 aestimatus 提供了后来法语和英语借用的形式。

items.en: Estimer and the past participle estimé pass into English as estimate.
items.cn: 法语 estimer 与过去分词 estimé 进入英语，成为 estimate。

items.en: Estimate is used as both verb and noun, and learns the prefix over-.
items.cn: estimate 同时用作动词与名词，并开始与前缀 over- 结合。

items.en: Overestimate is recorded as a verb meaning to set too high a value.
items.cn: 十八世纪记录到 overestimate 作动词，意为把价值估得过高。

items.en: Statistics, forecasting, and self-assessment make overestimate a common academic word.
items.cn: 在统计学、预测与自我评估中，overestimate 成为常见学术用词。

note.en: Overestimate is a Latin-rooted estimate under the prefix over-, paired everywhere with its mirror word underestimate.
note.cn: overestimate 是以拉丁词根 estimate 为核心的 over- 复合词，处处与它的镜像词 underestimate 成对出现。

entries.definition: to judge an amount roughly
entries.definitionCN: 估计；估算；去掉 over- 后的基础词

entries.definition: to judge as less than it is
entries.definitionCN: 低估；与 overestimate 前缀相反

entries.definition: the act or result of judging too high
entries.definitionCN: 高估；估计过高（名词形式）

entries.definition: to describe something as bigger than it is
entries.definitionCN: 夸大；夸张

entries.definition: to say something is larger than it is
entries.definitionCN: 夸大；言过其实

entries.definition: to judge wrongly, often by a wrong figure
entries.definitionCN: 计算错误；判断失误

normalIntro.en: Overestimate is an estimate pushed over the true line by the prefix over-.
normalIntro.cn: overestimate 就是被前缀 over- 推到真实值之上的一次估计。

normal.en: Over- means too much, as in overflow and overpay.
normal.cn: 前缀 over- 表示过多，如 overflow（溢出）和 overpay（多付）。

normal.en: Estimate means to work out roughly how much.
normal.cn: estimate 表示粗略地估算有多少。

normal.en: Put them together and you value something too high.
normal.cn: 两者相加，就是把某事物的价值或数量估得过高。

normal.en: Its mirror is underestimate, with under- for too little.
normal.cn: 它的镜像词是 underestimate，用 under- 表示过少。

normal.en: Overestimation is the noun, made with -ion from the verb.
normal.cn: overestimation 是名词，由动词加词尾 -ion 构成。

abstract.en: Picture a scale whose left pan sinks because a hidden weight was added.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平左盘下沉，因为被人偷偷加了砝码。

abstract.en: See a small team given a mountain of work on a whiteboard.
abstract.cn: 看见白板上给一个小团队写下一座山般的任务。

abstract.en: Imagine a chart bar drawn far above the real line.
abstract.cn: 想象图表里的柱子被画得远超真实刻度线。

examples.en: People often overestimate how little time a simple task takes.
examples.cn: 人们常常高估做一件小事所需的时间之短。

examples.en: Planners overestimated the number of cars that would use the road.
examples.cn: 规划者高估了会使用这条路的汽车数量。

examples.en: Do not overestimate your strength on the first hill.
examples.cn: 第一座山坡上别高估自己的体力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧弗-碎斯提-美特」——over（超过）加上听起来像「估」的 estimate，就是把数「估过头」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评值）→ aestimatus → 法语 estimer → 英语 estimate（估计）+ 前缀 over-（超过）→ overestimate（高估）。

sensesIntro.en: Overestimate moves from a number guessed too high, to a person judged too capable, to the too-high judgement itself.
sensesIntro.cn: overestimate 从「把数字估得过大」，到「把人看得过强」，再到「那个过高的估计本身」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an estimate placed above the true level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次估计被放在真实水平之上。

branches.en: A number judged too high is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 把数字判得过大是最常见的义项。

branches.en: The same extra weight applied to people becomes a judgement about ability.
branches.cn: 把这份多出的分量用在人身上，就变成对能力的判断。

branches.en: The act and its result share one form as a noun.
branches.cn: 行为与结果以名词形式共用一种拼写。

branches.en: A wrong figure and a too-high estimate are the same thing seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 错误的数字与过高的估计是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: Counting a crowd and judging a team both require putting a value on something.
branches.cn: 清点人群与评判团队都需要给事物一个估值。

intro.en: Overestimate is the Latin verb estimate behind the Germanic prefix over-, and its family runs from estimate to underestimation.
intro.cn: overestimate 是日耳曼语系前缀 over- 加拉丁词根动词 estimate，其词族从 estimate 一直延伸到 underestimation。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is aestimare, to value or appraise, with aestimatus and aestimatio as its derived forms.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁核心是 aestimare（估价、评值），派生形式有 aestimatus 与 aestimatio。

items.example: The prefix over- means too high in overestimate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 在 overestimate 中表示「过高」。

items.example: Estimate carries the Latin valuing image.
items.exampleCN: estimate 承载拉丁语「估价」的意象。

items.example: Overestimate is the full word.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 就是整个词。

items.example: The prefix under- forms underestimate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 构成 underestimate。

items.meaning: forming nouns of action or result
items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为或结果的名词
items.example: The suffix -ation forms estimation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 estimation。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms overestimated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 overestimated。

items.meaningCN: 第三人称单数或复数词尾
items.example: Overestimates is both a verb form and a plural.
items.exampleCN: overestimates 既是动词形式，也是复数。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms overestimating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overestimating。

items.example: Aestimare is the source of estimate.
items.exampleCN: aestimare 是 estimate 的源头。

items.example: Aestimatio predicts the English noun estimation.
items.exampleCN: aestimatio 预示了英语名词 estimation。

definition_zh: 装得过满；灌得太满；把（空间）塞得过满
definition_en: to put so much into a container or space that it is too full
core_image: 往玻璃杯里一直倒水，水面鼓出杯口，眼看就要顺着杯壁流下来
scene: 出发前的清晨，水壶被灌得太满，盖子一扣，水就从壶嘴往外挤。The morning went fine until he overfilled the kettle and it boiled over.
sceneCN: 这里 overfill 是「装得过满、灌得太满」（第 1 个义项：往容器里放入超出容量的东西）；句意为清晨一切顺利，直到他把水壶灌得太满，水沸后溢了出来。

pos.zh: 把……装得过满；灌得太满；塞得过满
过满；超量装填

derivatives.zh: over- 加 full 构成，形容「装得太满的；过满的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「装得过满的；塞得满满的」
反义对照：把空的补足、补充

senses.title: To put too much into a container
senses.definition: to put more liquid or material into a container than it can safely hold
senses.definitionCN: 往容器里放入超出其安全容量的液体或材料
senses.example: Do not overfill the bottle when you add the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 加油时不要把瓶子装得太满。
senses.why: Over- says beyond the limit and fill says make full, so the verb simply pushes full past full.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示「超过」，fill 表示「装满」，于是这个词就是让「满」再越过界限。

senses.title: To cram a space too full
senses.definition: to put too many people or things into a room, vehicle or other space
senses.definitionCN: 把过多的人或东西放进房间、车辆等空间
senses.example: The old bus was overfilled with passengers during rush hour.
senses.exampleCN: 高峰时段那辆旧公交车里挤满了乘客。
senses.why: The idea of excess moves from liquid to anything countable that fills a bounded space.
senses.whyCN: 「过量」这一观念从液体扩展到任何能填满有限空间的东西。

senses.title: A container that cannot take more
senses.definition: to become too full to hold anything more
senses.definitionCN: 变得太满，再也装不下任何东西
senses.example: The bin overfills quickly in a kitchen that never sorts its waste.
senses.exampleCN: 在从不分类厨余的厨房里，垃圾桶很快就被塞满。
senses.why: The same excess can be viewed from the container side, as a state rather than as someone acting.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「过量」也可以从容器这一面来看，于是它成为一种状态，而非某人的动作。

intro.en: Overfill is a transparent compound of the prefix over- and the verb fill, which goes back to Middle English fyllen and Old English fyllan.
intro.cn: overfill 由前缀 over- 与动词 fill 直接复合而成；fill 源自中古英语 fyllen，向上可追到古英语 fyllan。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as *fullijan, a causative built on the adjective meaning full.
items.cn: 通常把它构拟为 *fullijan，这是在表示「满」的形容词基础上构成的使役动词。

items.en: Old English fyllan means to make full, to fill, and also to complete.
items.cn: 古英语 fyllan 意为「使满、装满」，并有「完成」之意。

items.en: The prefix over- already meant above or beyond in Old English.
items.cn: 前缀 over- 在古英语中就已经表示「在上、超出」。

items.en: Middle English fyllen keeps the verb alive, and the spelling fill becomes standard later.
items.cn: 中古英语 fyllen 沿用这个动词，拼写 fill 后来才成为标准。

items.en: Overfill becomes common in the nineteenth century, and its first recorded date is uncertain.
items.cn: overfill 到十九世纪才通行，确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The verb now runs from kettles and fuel tanks to crowded buses and inboxes.
items.cn: 今天这个词从水壶、油箱延伸到拥挤的公交车和收件箱。

note.en: Overfill sits in the over- family, whose members all stress excess, and it stands beside the everyday verbs that describe something reaching its limit.
note.cn: overfill 属于表示「过量」的 over- 词族，并与描述事情到达极限的日常动词相邻。

entries.definition: too full to hold more
entries.definitionCN: 过满的：同一 over- 词族，由形容词 full 构成

entries.definition: to put too much of something onto a person or vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 使超载；使负担过重：共享 over- 前缀，但词根是 load

entries.definition: containing too many people
entries.definitionCN: 过于拥挤的：共享 over- 前缀，用于人群而非液体

entries.definition: to fill a place with water so that it covers it
entries.definitionCN: 淹没；被水灌满：强调后果是覆盖，而不仅是装不下

entries.definition: to push too much into a space by force
entries.definitionCN: 塞满；硬塞：强调用力往里压动作

entries.definition: to push things into a bag or space very quickly
entries.definitionCN: 塞满；填塞：强调匆匆填放，不必然过量

normalIntro.en: Overfill is a two-piece word: over- means beyond the limit and fill means make full.
normalIntro.cn: overfill 可以拆成两半：over- 表示「超过界限」，fill 表示「装满」。

normal.en: Over- appears in overload, oversleep and overeat, all showing excess.
normal.cn: over- 也出现在 overload、oversleep、overeat 里，都表示「过量」。

normal.en: Fill and full share one root: to fill is to make something full.
normal.cn: fill 与 full 同根：fill 就是使某物变满。

normal.en: The noun overfill is the amount that could not fit in.
normal.cn: 名词 overfill 指装不下的那一部分。

normal.en: Fuel stations warn drivers not to overfill the tank before a long trip.
normal.cn: 加油站提醒司机长途出行前不要把油箱加得过满。

normal.en: Compare overfull, the adjective for something that is already too full.
normal.cn: 对比形容词 overfull，它形容某物已经太满的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a cup where the water rises above the rim in a trembling dome.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水高出杯口，鼓成颤抖的水面。

abstract.en: See a bus door that cannot close because one more passenger is pushed in.
abstract.cn: 想象公交车门关不上，因为又挤进去了一名乘客。

abstract.en: Think of a bin with the lid open, waste spilling onto the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象垃圾桶盖开着，垃圾已经洒到地上。

examples.en: He overfilled the sink and the water ran onto the tiles.
examples.cn: 他把水槽灌得太满，水漫到了瓷砖上。

examples.en: Never overfill a fuel tank on a hot day.
examples.cn: 天热时绝不要把油箱加得过满。

examples.en: The drawers were overfilled with old tickets and receipts.
examples.cn: 抽屉里塞满了旧车票和收据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧福菲尔」——欧式的杯子装满还要再凑菲尔一杯；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 前缀 over-（古英语，表示「在上、超出」）+ 动词 fill（源自中古英语 fyllen，更早为古英语 fyllan，使役构拟 *fullijan）→ 现代英语 overfill（装得过满），核心义「让满越过界限」。

sensesIntro.en: Overfill begins with liquid overflowing a container, then spreads to crowded spaces, and finally names the state of a container that can take no more.
sensesIntro.cn: overfill 先指液体把容器灌得溢出来，再扩展到拥挤的空间，最后指容器装不下任何东西的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rising above the rim of a glass and spilling down the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面高出杯口，顺着杯壁流下。

branches.en: Liquid in a container is the most concrete branch.
branches.cn: 容器里的液体是最具体的分支。

branches.en: People and goods packed into a space carry the same excess.
branches.cn: 挤进空间的人和货物承载着同样的过量。

branches.en: The container side of the same event becomes a state.
branches.cn: 同一事件的容器一面成为状态义。

branches.en: Both senses start from a bounded capacity that is exceeded.
branches.cn: 两个义项都始于一个被突破的有限容量。

branches.en: A verb and a state describe the same overflowing container.
branches.cn: 动词与状态描述的是同一个被灌满的容器。

intro.en: Overfill is built from the prefix over- and the free verb fill, and the family below covers its parts and its nearest neighbours.
intro.cn: overfill 由前缀 over- 与自由动词 fill 构成，下列构词条目涵盖它的组成部分和最接近的邻里词。

latinIntro.en: Overfill has no Latin source: both parts are native English, so the Latin entries here are empty.
latinIntro.cn: overfill 没有拉丁语来源，两部分都是英语本族成分，因此这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Over- turns a neutral word into one of excess.
items.exampleCN: over- 把中性词变成表示过量的词。

items.example: Fill is the base verb of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fill 是整个词族的基础动词。

items.example: Full is the adjective behind the verb fill.
items.exampleCN: full 是动词 fill 背后的那个形容词。

items.example: Fyllan is the Old English source of fill.
items.exampleCN: fyllan 是 fill 的古英语源头。

items.example: Over- plus full gives overfull.
items.exampleCN: over- 加 full 构成 overfull。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms overfilling from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 由动词构成 overfilling。

items.example: Overload shows the same over- pattern.
items.exampleCN: overload 体现了同样的 over- 构词模式。

items.example: Overflow is what happens after you overfill.
items.exampleCN: overflow 是装得过满之后发生的事。

definition_zh: 溢出；漫出；挤满；（情感）洋溢
definition_en: to flow over the edge of a container or place because there is too much of something
core_image: 河水涨到堤岸顶，越过岸沿，一路漫到草地上
scene: 连日的雨过后，河边的排水沟再也装不下水，污水漫过路面流进低处的房子。After three days of rain, the river began to overflow and the road was soon under water.
sceneCN: 这里 overflow 是「溢出、漫出」（第 1 个义项：液体过多而越过边界）；句意为下了三天雨后，河水开始溢出，路面很快被淹。

pos.zh: 溢出；漫出；挤满；（情感）洋溢
溢出物；溢流口；超出部分的量

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 作形容词，义为「满得溢出的；洋溢的」
古旧或文学用法的过去分词形式，表示「被淹过的」
近义对照：以淹没为结果，不强调越过边沿

senses.title: Liquid flowing over an edge
senses.definition: to flow over the top edge of a container, river or other boundary
senses.definitionCN: 液体越过容器、河流等物的顶端边沿流出去
senses.example: The bath overflowed while nobody was watching.
senses.exampleCN: 没人看的时候，浴缸的水溢了出来。
senses.why: Over- means over the edge and flow means move like liquid, so the verb is liquid crossing a boundary.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示「越过边沿」，flow 表示「像液体一样流动」，所以这个词就是液体越过边界。

senses.title: A place too full for those arriving
senses.definition: to be filled beyond capacity, so that extra people or things spill elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 被填得超出容量，于是多出来的人或物被挤到别处
senses.example: The hall overflowed into the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅挤得站不下，人流涌到了走廊里。
senses.why: The image of liquid spilling is applied to crowds, which press out of a crowded room.
senses.whyCN: 液体外溢的画面被移用到人群上，人们从拥挤的房间里被挤出来。

senses.title: Feeling that spills over
senses.definition: to be so full of a feeling that it shows openly
senses.definitionCN: 某种情感满得外露出来
senses.example: She overflowed with gratitude when the neighbours helped her move.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居帮她搬家时，她满怀感激。
senses.why: An inner store can also reach its limit, and emotion flows out like water.
senses.whyCN: 内心的藏量也会到达极限，情感便像水一样流了出来。

senses.title: The kept amount that does not fit
senses.definition: the extra liquid or data that is caught or stored when a container is full
senses.definitionCN: 容器满了之后被接住或另外存放的多余液体或数据
senses.example: The tank has an overflow that carries excess water into a drain.
senses.exampleCN: 水箱有一个溢流口，把多余的水送进下水道。
senses.why: Once the event is understood, engineers name the excess itself, and computing borrows the same idea for data.
senses.whyCN: 弄懂这一现象后，工程师用它来命名多出来的那部分；计算机领域也借用同一概念来指数据。

senses.title: A system reaching its limit
senses.definition: to exceed the capacity of a system, place or budget, so that some part has to wait or move
senses.definitionCN: 超出系统、场所或预算的容量，以至于某部分必须等待或转移
senses.example: Messages overflowed the server within a minute of the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 上线仅一分钟，消息就挤爆了服务器。
senses.why: Any bounded system repeats the image of a full container pressing against its wall.
senses.whyCN: 任何有边界的系统都在重复「满容器顶向四壁」的画面。

intro.en: Overflow joins the prefix over- to the verb flow, which comes from Old English flowan, also recorded as flōwan, a verb of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: overflow 由前缀 over- 与动词 flow 结合而成；flow 源自古英语 flowan，也记作 flōwan，属日耳曼语系动词。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as *flōwan, generally linked to a root for flowing or swimming.
items.cn: 一般把它构拟为 *flōwan，并与表示「流动、游泳」的词根相联系。

items.en: Old English flowan means to flow, run or move like water.
items.cn: 古英语 flowan 意为「流动、流淌、像水那样移动」。

items.en: The compound already appears in Old English with the sense of running over.
items.cn: 这个复合词在古英语中就已出现，义为「漫溢」。

items.en: Middle English spells both flowen and overflowen, and the noun overflow follows.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 flowen 与 overflowen，名词 overflow 也随之出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded from about the fifteenth century, though exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词约自十五世纪有记录，确切年代不确定。

items.en: Overflow spreads to crowds, feelings, car parks and computer memory.
items.cn: overflow 后来扩展到人群、情感、停车场和计算机内存。

note.en: Overflow names liquid or data crossing a boundary, so it sits between the over- family and the flood words.
note.cn: overflow 指液体或数据越过边界，因此它处在 over- 词族与「淹没」类词之间。

entries.definition: to move steadily like water
entries.definitionCN: 流动：flood 与 flow 同根，都是最基础的水流动词

entries.definition: to put too much into a container
entries.definitionCN: 装得过满：共享 over- 前缀，常是 overflow 的原因

entries.definition: to put too much onto something or someone
entries.definitionCN: 使超载：共享 over- 前缀，词根为 load 而非 flow

entries.definition: to cover a place with a large amount of water
entries.definitionCN: 淹没：强调被水覆盖的结果，而非越过边沿这一动作

entries.definition: to let liquid fall out of a container
entries.definitionCN: 洒出：常含意外地弄翻之意

entries.definition: to be full to the top edge
entries.definitionCN: 满到边沿：多用于形容满而未溢出

normalIntro.en: Overflow is two clear parts: over- says beyond the edge and flow says the liquid is moving.
normalIntro.cn: overflow 可以清楚拆成两半：over- 表示「越过边沿」，flow 表示液体在流动。

normal.en: Over- appears in overrun, overspill and overhang, all involving something beyond a limit.
normal.cn: over- 也出现在 overrun、overspill、overhang 里，都含「超出界限」之意。

normal.en: The noun overflow names the extra amount, as in an overflow pipe.
normal.cn: 名词 overflow 指多出来的那一部分，如溢流管。

normal.en: In computing, buffer overflow happens when stored data exceeds a set size.
normal.cn: 计算机里的 buffer overflow 指存放的数据超出预定容量。

normal.en: Overflow with means to be full of a feeling, as in overflowing with joy.
normal.cn: overflow with 表示充满某种情感，如 overflowing with joy 意为「满心欢喜」。

normal.en: Compare fill, which only says make full, while overflow says full and then moving past.
normal.cn: 对比 fill：它只说「装满」，overflow 则说满之后还越了过去。

abstract.en: Picture a river rising until it slides over the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象河水上涨，直到翻过堤岸。

abstract.en: See a cup on a table with a shining pool of tea around it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一只杯子，四周是一圈发亮的茶水。

abstract.en: Think of a hall so crowded that people stand in the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大厅挤得满人，多出来的人站到了走廊里。

examples.en: The river overflowed after the storm and closed the bridge.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后河水溢出，桥梁被迫封闭。

examples.en: Her joy seemed to overflow when she saw the results.
examples.cn: 看到结果时，她的喜悦满得溢了出来。

examples.en: Please keep the tank below the overflow mark.
examples.cn: 请把水箱的水位保持在溢流线以下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃弗楼」——欧式的楼里水一直流，流过门槛就是溢出；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 前缀 over-（古英语，表示「越过、超出」）+ 动词 flow（古英语 flowan，一般构拟自 *flōwan，意为「流动」）→ 古英语 overflowan → 现代英语 overflow（溢出），核心义「水流越过边界」。

sensesIntro.en: Overflow starts with liquid crossing an edge, grows to crowded places and feelings, then names the excess itself and finally any system pushed past its limit.
sensesIntro.cn: overflow 从液体越过边界开始，扩展到拥挤的场所和情感，再指多出来的那部分，最后指任何超出限度的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river sliding over its bank and spreading across the field.
core.cn: 核心意象：河水翻过堤岸，漫上田地。

branches.en: Liquid crossing an edge is the literal core.
branches.cn: 液体越过边沿是本义核心。

branches.en: Crowds and feelings are inner or social volumes that cannot stay contained.
branches.cn: 人群和情感都是无法被容纳的内在与外在容量。

branches.en: The process is turned into a name for what is kept back.
branches.cn: 这一过程被用来命名被保留下的多余部分。

branches.en: Any bounded system pushed past capacity repeats the image.
branches.cn: 任何被推过容量的有界系统都在重复这一画面。

branches.en: The flowing event and the extra amount are two faces of one image.
branches.cn: 流动的事件与多出的份额是同一意象的两面。

intro.en: Overflow is built from the prefix over- and the verb flow, a native Germanic verb; the family below shows its parts and its close neighbours.
intro.cn: overflow 由前缀 over- 与动词 flow 构成，flow 是本族日耳曼语动词；下列构词条目展示其成分与近邻词。

latinIntro.en: Overflow has no Latin origin: both parts are Old English, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: overflow 没有拉丁语来源，两部分都出自古英语，因此拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Over- signals something crossing a limit.
items.exampleCN: over- 表示某物越过界限。

items.example: Flow is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: flow 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Flowan is the Old English source of flow.
items.exampleCN: flowan 是 flow 的古英语源头。

items.example: Overflowan already carried the modern meaning.
items.exampleCN: overflowan 已具备现代含义。

items.example: Flood shares the Germanic water-root.
items.exampleCN: flood 共享日耳曼语的水流词根。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives overflowing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overflowing。

items.meaning: excess that must be moved elsewhere
items.example: Overspill shows the same over- pattern.
items.exampleCN: overspill 体现同样的 over- 构词模式。

items.example: Overrun repeats the beyond-the-limit idea.
items.exampleCN: overrun 重复了「越界」的观念。

definition_zh: 过度放牧；在（草地）上过度放牧
definition_en: to let farm animals eat so much grass in a place that the plants cannot recover
core_image: 一群羊在同一个坡上啃草，草被啃到贴地，露出光秃秃的土
scene: 山坡上，牧人为了多养几只羊，让羊群在同一块草场上反复吃草，草渐渐连根都被啃掉了。Farmers who overgraze the hills soon see the soil wash away in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 overgraze 是「过度放牧」（第 1 个义项：牲畜吃草量超过草地恢复能力）；句意为把山坡过度放牧的农户，很快就会发现雨水把土壤冲走了。

pos.zh: 在（某处）过度放牧；使（草地）因放牧过度而退化
（牲畜）放牧过度

collocations.zh: 在同一片土地上过度放牧

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 名词化，指「过度放牧」这一行为与后果
基础动词，「吃草、放牧」；加上 over- 后才含过量之意
过度放养或囤积，常与过度放牧相伴出现

senses.title: To feed animals beyond what the land can support
senses.definition: to keep so many animals on a piece of land that the grass is eaten away and cannot grow back
senses.definitionCN: 在同一片土地上饲养过多牲畜，草被啃光，再也长不回来
senses.example: Farmers were asked not to overgraze the hills in dry years.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱年份里，人们要求农户不要把山坡放牧过度。
senses.why: Over- adds excess and graze names the eating of grass, so the act of feeding goes past what the land can renew.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示「过量」，graze 表示「吃草、放牧」，于是放牧就远远超出了土地能自行恢复的程度。

senses.title: A hill or field stripped bare
senses.definition: to eat away the plant cover of a place so that only bare soil is left
senses.definitionCN: 把某处的植被啃光，只剩下裸露的土壤
senses.example: The slope was overgrazed and now turns to dust in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 这片坡地被啃得精光，如今风一吹就成尘土。
senses.why: The same excess can be described from the land side, where the result is bare ground.
senses.whyCN: 同样的过量也可以从土地这一面来描述，其结果是光秃的地面。

senses.title: The ecological damage that follows
senses.definition: to cause long-lasting damage to soil and plants through repeated heavy grazing
senses.definitionCN: 因反复重度放牧而使土壤和植被受到长期损害
senses.example: Deserts expand where people overgraze fragile land for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 在人们多年过度放牧脆弱土地的地方，沙漠不断扩大。
senses.why: Once the image is an ecological one, a short act of grazing becomes a long chain of erosion and desertification.
senses.whyCN: 一旦进入生态语境，短期的放牧行为就发展成侵蚀与荒漠化的漫长链条。

intro.en: Overgraze is a modern compound of the prefix over- and the verb graze, a Germanic word for the eating of grass. The verb graze of grazing animals and the unrelated verb graze of a small graze wound are different words; the one meant here is the feeding word.
intro.cn: overgraze 是前缀 over- 与动词 graze 的现代复合词；graze 表示「吃草」，是日耳曼语词。这里要说明：牲畜吃草的 graze 与「擦伤」的 graze 只是拼写相同，来源不同。

items.en: The feeding verb graze is recorded in Middle English greysen, with related forms in other Germanic languages; deeper origins are uncertain.
items.cn: 表示「吃草」的 graze 在中古英语中记作 greysen，在其他日耳曼语言里也有相关形式；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The prefix over- already meant above or beyond in Old English.
items.cn: 前缀 over- 在古英语中已经表示「在上、超出」。

items.en: The feeding verb settles on the spelling graze in Middle English.
items.cn: 表示「吃草」的动词在中古英语里定形为拼写 graze。

items.en: Overgraze and overgrazing join village records and farming guides; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: overgraze 与 overgrazing 出现在乡村记录和农事指南中；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Ecology makes overgrazing a standard term for a form of land degradation.
items.cn: 生态学把 overgrazing 确立为「土地退化」的标准术语。

items.en: Today the word appears in climate and desertification reports.
items.cn: 今天这个词常出现在气候与荒漠化报告中。

note.en: Overgraze belongs to the over- family and to the grassland vocabulary, where grazing, browsing and stocking set different limits on land.
note.cn: overgraze 属于 over- 词族，也属于草原词汇；在那里，放牧、采食和载畜量各自设定了不同的土地界限。

entries.definition: to eat grass in a field
entries.definitionCN: 吃草；放牧：基础动词，加上 over- 才表示过量；另有一个同拼写的「擦伤」义，词源不同

entries.definition: the practice or result of grazing too heavily
entries.definitionCN: 过度放牧：动名词形式，常作生态学术语使用

entries.definition: to take too much of a natural resource
entries.definitionCN: 过度采捕：共享 over- 前缀，对象从草变为渔获或林木

entries.definition: to eat leaves and shoots from bushes
entries.definitionCN: 啃食灌木枝叶：与吃草并列为牲畜采食方式

entries.definition: to wear away soil or rock gradually
entries.definitionCN: 侵蚀：过度放牧之后最常见的后果

entries.definition: to keep farm animals on a piece of land
entries.definitionCN: 放养牲畜：overstock 与 overgraze 常同时出现

normalIntro.en: Overgraze is over- plus graze: too many animals, too little grass, and the ground left bare.
normalIntro.cn: overgraze 就是 over- 加 graze：牲畜太多、草太少，最后地面光秃。

normal.en: Graze and grass start alike: grazing animals eat the grass.
normal.cn: graze 与 grass 开头相同：放牧的牲畜把草吃光。

normal.en: Over- appears in overuse, overfish and overgraze, all meaning using more than can be replaced.
normal.cn: over- 也出现在 overuse、overfish、overgraze 里，都表示「用得超过可恢复的量」。

normal.en: The noun overgrazing is the standard term in reports on soil erosion.
normal.cn: 名词 overgrazing 是土壤侵蚀报告中的标准说法。

normal.en: Note that graze also means to scrape the skin; that sense has a different origin.
normal.cn: 注意 graze 还可指「擦破皮」，那一义来源不同。

normal.en: Compare overharvest, which applies the same excess to fish and timber rather than grass.
normal.cn: 对比 overharvest：同样的「过量」用在渔获或林木上，而非草。

abstract.en: Picture a hill where every sheep is chewing the same patch of green.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山坡上，每只羊都在啃同一小片绿草。

abstract.en: See grass eaten down to the soil, with stones showing through.
abstract.cn: 想象草被啃到泥土，石块露了出来。

abstract.en: Think of a report map that marks a dusty region in red.
abstract.cn: 想象报告地图上用红色标出的沙化区域。

examples.en: The valley was overgrazed for decades before the soil began to fail.
examples.cn: 这个山谷被过度放牧了几十年，土壤才开始退化。

examples.en: Goats will overgraze a small field within a single season.
examples.cn: 山羊在一季之内就能把一小块地啃得精光。

examples.en: Scientists link the lost grassland to years of overgrazing.
examples.cn: 科学家把草原的消失与多年的过度放牧联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃格瑞兹」——欧式的草场被格瑞啃到只剩土渣；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 前缀 over-（古英语，表示「在上、超出」）+ 动词 graze（中古英语 greysen，表示牲畜吃草，属日耳曼语源，更早来源不确定）→ 现代英语 overgraze（过度放牧），核心义「让牲畜吃草超过土地能恢复的量」。

sensesIntro.en: Overgraze begins with a farming act, then moves to the stripped land that results, and finally to the long ecological damage.
sensesIntro.cn: overgraze 从一种农事行为开始，再转到被啃光的土地，最后指向长期的生态损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheep chewing the same hill until only bare soil is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：羊群反复啃同一片坡，直到只剩裸土。

branches.en: The act of feeding too many animals is the human branch.
branches.cn: 养太多牲畜让它吃草是人的行为分支。

branches.en: The land side shows only bare ground.
branches.cn: 土地一面只呈现光秃的地面。

branches.en: Ecology turns the act into slow damage that outlasts the animals.
branches.cn: 生态学把这一行为转成比牲畜更持久的缓慢损害。

branches.en: Act and result describe the same hill in one season.
branches.cn: 行为与结果描述的是同一季里的同一片坡地。

branches.en: Bare soil is the moment when erosion becomes visible.
branches.cn: 裸土露出的那一刻，侵蚀开始变得可见。

intro.en: Overgraze is built from the prefix over- and the verb graze; the family below shows its parts and its close neighbours in grassland vocabulary.
intro.cn: overgraze 由前缀 over- 与动词 graze 构成；下列构词条目展示它的组成部分以及草原词汇中的近邻词。

latinIntro.en: Overgraze has no Latin origin: over- and graze are both Germanic, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: overgraze 没有拉丁语来源，over- 与 graze 都属日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Over- turns graze into overgraze.
items.exampleCN: over- 把 graze 变成 overgraze。

items.example: Graze is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: graze 是该词族的基础动词。

items.example: Greysen is the Middle English source of graze.
items.exampleCN: greysen 是 graze 的中古英语源头。

items.example: Grass names the food that grazing consumes.
items.exampleCN: grass 指明放牧所消耗的食物。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms overgrazing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overgrazing。

items.example: Pasture is the place where grazing happens.
items.exampleCN: pasture 是放牧发生的地方。

items.example: A herd that is too large overgrazes a field.
items.exampleCN: 畜群过大就会把草地放牧过度。

items.example: Overfish follows the same over- pattern.
items.exampleCN: overfish 遵循同样的 over- 构词模式。

definition_zh: 使狂喜；使极度高兴；使大喜过望
definition_en: to fill someone with such great joy that it goes beyond the ordinary
core_image: 一个人听到好消息后原地蹦起，双手不知往哪放
scene: 录取通知寄到家里，母亲一边读一边掉眼泪，父亲连声道贺。Nobody in the family could sleep the night they were overjoyed by the news of the scholarship.
sceneCN: 这里 overjoy 是「使大喜过望、欣喜若狂」（第 1 个义项：被极度快乐淹没）；此处用被动式 overjoyed，表示全家人被奖学金的消息弄得过分高兴，句意：奖学金消息传到的那晚，家里没有人睡得着。

pos.zh: 使狂喜；使极度高兴；使大喜过望

derivatives.zh: over 表「过度」加 joy 的过去分词，义为「狂喜的；大喜过望的」，是现代英语最常用的形式
基础名词，义为「欢乐；喜悦」，overjoy 正是由它加前缀构成
joy 加 -ful（充满……的），义为「快乐的；令人愉快的」，语气平常，不如 overjoyed 强烈
joy 加 -ous（具有……性质的），义为「充满喜乐的」，多用于书面语与节庆描写
joyful 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「欢快地；兴高采烈地」

senses.title: To fill someone with excessive joy
senses.definition: to make someone extremely happy, so that the feeling goes beyond what is usual
senses.definitionCN: 使某人极其快乐，快乐的程度超出寻常
senses.example: The news overjoyed the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让全村人欣喜若狂。
senses.why: The prefix over- means beyond or too much, so overjoying someone means pouring more joy into a person than the ordinary measure.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「超过、过度」，所以使人被过量的喜悦灌满，就是「使狂喜」；核心画面是快乐溢出了平时的杯子。

senses.title: Feeling overwhelmed by joy
senses.definition: the state of being so full of joy that a person can hardly contain the feeling
senses.definitionCN: 内心充满喜悦、几乎无法自持的状态
senses.example: She was overjoyed when her team won the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她的队伍赢得决赛时，她欣喜若狂。
senses.why: The particle over- can also mark an overpowering state, so the past participle overjoyed becomes a description of someone completely taken over by joy.
senses.whyCN: over- 还可以表示「压倒性的状态」，于是过去分词 overjoyed 就用来形容一个人被喜悦完全占据，对应「欣喜若狂」这一状态义。

senses.title: Joy beyond expectation
senses.definition: to make someone happier than they had expected to be
senses.definitionCN: 使某人比原本预想的更高兴
senses.example: The result overjoyed the players, who had expected to lose.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结果让原本以为会输的球员们喜出望外。
senses.why: Over- can mean passing the expected line, so overjoyed describes a joy that shoots past what a person hoped for.
senses.whyCN: over- 有「越过某条界线」的意思，越过的是预期这条线，于是过度的高兴就变成了「喜出望外」的惊喜义。

senses.title: A brief burst of intense delight
senses.definition: a short, fierce rush of joy that arrives all at once, as if from the outside
senses.definitionCN: 突然袭来、一阵猛烈而短暂的喜悦，仿佛从外部冲进心里
senses.example: The news overjoyed him for a moment before worry set in.
senses.exampleCN: 这一消息先让他一阵狂喜，随后忧虑才涌上来。
senses.why: Because overjoying is a force acting on a person, it pictures joy arriving as a blow or wave instead of a quiet background feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为使人狂喜是一种从外部作用于人的力量，所以这个动词的画面是喜悦像一阵浪一样扑上来，而不是静静的好心情。

senses.title: Rejoicing with someone
senses.definition: to share or spread the delight of another person, so that others become joyful too
senses.definitionCN: 分享或传递他人的喜悦，使别人也高兴起来
senses.example: Their loud cheering overjoyed the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们响亮的欢呼让邻居们也跟着高兴。
senses.why: The verb is transitive, so joy travels outward from one person into somebody else; overjoying becomes a social act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是及物动词，喜悦要从一个人身上流到另一个人身上，于是 overjoy 延伸出「与他人一同欢庆」的社会性用法。

senses.title: A warm, overflowing pleasure
senses.definition: a full, warm contentment in which joy keeps spilling over, felt calmly rather than wildly
senses.definitionCN: 一种充盈而温暖的满足欢欣，喜悦不断溢出，感受平静而不狂乱
senses.example: The first cuddle of the baby overjoyed the tired parents.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的第一次依偎让疲惫的父母心里满是暖洋洋的欢欣。
senses.why: Joy is a warm inner feeling, so the overflow image can also describe pleasure that spills over gently rather than violently.
senses.whyCN: joy 本身是温暖的内心感受，所以「溢出」的画面也可以描述轻轻漫出来的满足，对应不狂躁、暖洋洋的欢喜。

senses.title: Joy that overcomes sadness or fear
senses.definition: to relieve a person from sorrow or anxiety by bringing such great joy that the darker feeling is drowned
senses.definitionCN: 用极大的喜悦冲走悲伤或焦虑，让消极的情绪被喜悦压下去
senses.example: Seeing her brother alive overjoyed the old woman even as she wept.
senses.exampleCN: 看到弟弟还活着，老妇人喜极而泣，满心欢喜。
senses.why: Since the prefix over- can mean over and above, overjoying someone can mean bringing joy that lies above and covers grief.
senses.whyCN: over- 还有「覆于其上、超过」的意义，所以使人狂喜也可以指带来盖过悲伤的快乐，完成「以喜压忧、喜极而泣」这一义。

senses.title: Pleasure that is almost too much
senses.titleCN: 过于高兴；欢喜得有些失态
senses.definition: to be so elated that the joy feels excessive and a little out of control
senses.definitionCN: 高兴得过了头，喜悦显得过量、甚至有点失控
senses.example: The fans were overjoyed by the win, chanting for hours in the street.
senses.exampleCN: 球迷们因胜利而欢喜得失态，在街上连续唱了好几个小时。
senses.why: The prefix over- keeps its literal sense of too much, so the extreme end describes joy that has passed the point of being sensible.
senses.whyCN: over- 保留「过分」的字面意义，走到极端时就是快乐越过了得体的限度，这一义项把「过度」写到了负面的边缘。

intro.en: Overjoy joins the Old French prefix over- with the Latin-derived noun joy, which goes back to Latin gaudium and gaudere.
intro.cn: overjoy 由中古英语前缀 over-（过度）与源出拉丁语 gaudium 的名词 joy 组合而成，整体词形成于英语内部。

items.en: Gaudere means to be glad, and the noun gaudium means joy or gladness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaudere 意为「高兴」，名词 gaudium 意为「欢乐；喜悦」。

items.en: Joy, joie and the verb joir enter French from the Latin pleasure words.
items.cn: 古法语 joie（喜悦）与动词 joir 承自拉丁语，成为英语的输入来源。

items.en: The noun joy is borrowed from Old French and settled into English as the everyday word for gladness.
items.cn: 名词 joy 从中古英语时期由古法语借入，逐渐成为英语中表示「欢乐」的日常词。

items.en: The native prefix ofer- (over) already meant above or beyond, and it appears in many Middle English compounds.
items.cn: 源于古英语的前缀 ofer-（在上、越过）在中古英语中广泛用于构词，表示「过度」。

items.en: The verb overjoy is first recorded in the sixteenth century, very often in the passive form overjoyed.
items.cn: 动词 overjoy 据记录最早见于十六世纪，并以被动形式 overjoyed 最为常见。

items.en: The active verb grows rare while the adjective overjoyed remains the main everyday use.
items.cn: 在现代英语里，主动语态的动词已少见，而形容词 overjoyed 仍是主要用法。

note.en: Overjoy is built from over- and joy, and its neighbours are the joy family on one side and the rejoicing verbs on the other.
note.cn: overjoy 由 over- 与 joy 构成，一侧是 joy 词族，另一侧是表示「欢欣」的动词与形容词。

entries.definition: a feeling of great happiness
entries.definitionCN: joy 是 overjoy 的基础名词，义为「欢乐；喜悦」。

entries.definition: too much; excessively
entries.definitionCN: overly 与 overjoy 同样由 over- 表「过度」构成，义为「过于」；只是拼写相近，两者并非同一词根派生链上的同源词。

entries.definition: to do too much of something
entries.definitionCN: overdo 也是 over- 加动词的「做过量」，义为「做过头」。

entries.definition: to affect someone very strongly
entries.definitionCN: overwhelm 与 overjoy 构词平行，义为「使不堪承受」，只是拼写结构相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to give great pleasure
entries.definitionCN: delight 义为「使高兴；使愉悦」，快乐强烈但通常不含「过度」的意味。

entries.definition: to excite someone greatly
entries.definitionCN: thrill 义为「使激动」，强调一阵震颤般的兴奋。

entries.definition: to make someone feel very happy and proud
entries.definitionCN: elate 义为「使兴高采烈」，多用于描述得意与振奋。

entries.definition: to feel or show great joy
entries.definitionCN: rejoice 义为「欣喜；使欣喜」，是 joy 词族中常见的「欢欣」动词。

normalIntro.en: Overjoy is joy pushed beyond the usual mark by the prefix over-, so every sense grows from the idea of a cup that spills.
normalIntro.cn: overjoy 是 joy 被前缀 over- 推到寻常刻度之外，所有义项都从「杯子满到溢出」这个画面长出来。

normal.en: Over- in overjoy, overturn and overdo all point to going too far.
normal.cn: overjoy、overturn、overdo 中的 over- 都指「越过、过度」。

normal.en: The passive form overjoyed is far more common than the active verb.
normal.cn: 被动形式 overjoyed 比主动动词常见得多，记搭配时可以连着 be 一起记。

normal.en: Be overjoyed at the news and be overjoyed to hear are fixed frames.
normal.cn: be overjoyed at the news 与 be overjoyed to hear 都是固定搭配框架。

normal.en: Joy shares its Latin source gaudium with the adjective joyful.
normal.cn: joy 与形容词 joyful 共享拉丁语源头 gaudium，属于同一词族。

normal.en: Compare delight: delight is strong pleasure, overjoy adds the idea of too much.
normal.cn: 对比 delight：delight 是强烈的快乐，overjoy 额外带上「过量」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a champagne glass fizzing over the rim when good news arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象好消息传来时，一只香槟杯冒着泡沫溢出了杯缘。

abstract.en: Think of a child spinning round and round until joy tips into dizziness.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子转圈转到快乐翻成眩晕，这就是「过度」的喜悦。

abstract.en: See a wave of joy washing in over a person who expected nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵喜悦的浪，冲着毫无预期的人扑过来。

examples.en: The letter overjoyed the family, who had given up any hope of a reply.
examples.cn: 那封信让早已不指望回音的这家人欣喜万分。

examples.en: He was overjoyed to be offered the job in the mountain hospital.
examples.cn: 得到山区医院的工作机会，他欣喜若狂。

examples.en: Her overjoyed face at the airport told us the visa had finally come.
examples.cn: 她在机场那张喜出望外的脸说明签证终于到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧味jolli」——欧式的喜悦加倍涌上来，就是「狂喜」；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语内部构词：中古英语前缀 over-（源自更早的 ofer-，意为「在上、越过、过度」）+ 名词 joy（借自古法语 joie，源出拉丁语 gaudium「欢乐」，动词 gaudere「高兴」）。整个动词不是拉丁语原词，而是英语在十六世纪用本族前缀加借入名词拼合而成。

sensesIntro.en: Overjoy begins with the act of making someone excessively happy and then bends into the state of being overwhelmed, the surprise of joy beyond expectation, and finally joy that is plainly too much.
sensesIntro.cn: overjoy 从「使人大喜」这一动作出发，再转向「被喜悦淹没」的状态、超出预期的惊喜，最后落在明显的「高兴得过分」之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup of joy filled so full that it spills over the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯喜悦倒得太满，溢出了杯口。

branches.en: Making others joyful is the active core sense.
branches.cn: 使别人高兴是动作上的核心义项。

branches.en: Being overjoyed and being hit by a burst of delight are states felt from inside.
branches.cn: 「欣喜若狂」与「一阵狂喜的冲击」都是内在感受到的状态。

branches.en: Going beyond the expected line gives the surprise sense.
branches.cn: 越过预期这条界线，就得到「喜出望外」的惊喜义。

branches.en: Shared celebration, warm contentment and joy over grief show the overflow turning gentle or healing.
branches.cn: 同庆、暖意与以喜压忧展示出「溢出」转向温和或疗愈的一面。

branches.en: The literal sense of too much ends the chain with joy out of control.
branches.cn: 字面的「过度」落到链尾，就是欢喜得失控的一义。

intro.en: Overjoy is a transparent English compound: the prefix over- adds excess to the noun joy, and most modern use lives in the adjective overjoyed.
intro.cn: overjoy 是构词透明的英语复合词：前缀 over- 给名词 joy 加上「过度」的意味，现代英语里绝大多数用法落在形容词 overjoyed 上。

latinIntro.en: The joy part goes back through Old French joie to Latin gaudium, from the verb gaudere, to be glad.
latinIntro.cn: joy 这一部分经古法语 joie 上溯到拉丁语 gaudium（欢乐），动词形式是 gaudere（高兴）；over- 则是英语本族前缀，与拉丁语无关。

items.example: Over- in overjoy means too much joy.
items.exampleCN: overjoy 中的 over- 表示「过度的」喜悦。

items.example: Joy is the borrowed noun inside overjoy.
items.exampleCN: joy 是 overjoy 内部借入的名词。

items.example: Gaudere is the distant root of joy.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 joy 的远源。

items.example: Gaudium passes into Old French as joie.
items.exampleCN: gaudium 传入古法语成为 joie。

items.example: Joie is the Old French form borrowed into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: joie 是被中古英语借入的古法语形式。

items.example: The past participle overjoyed is the everyday form.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词 overjoyed 是日常最常用的形式。

items.example: The suffix -ed turns the verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: Joyful adds -ful to the same noun.
items.exampleCN: joyful 是在同一名词上加 -ful 构成。

items.example: Joyous adds -ous to the same noun.
items.exampleCN: joyous 是在同一名词上加 -ous 构成。

items.example: The adverb joyfully adds -ly to joyful.
items.exampleCN: 副词 joyfully 由 joyful 加 -ly 构成。

definition_zh: 覆盖在……之上；压在……上面；放在……之上；位于……上层
definition_en: to lie on top of something and partly or wholly cover it
core_image: 一张毯子平铺在地面之上，四边自然垂下
scene: 地质课上，老师指着剖面图中间的灰色岩层，说明它上面压着更年轻的沉积物。In the diagram, a layer of limestone overlies the darker shale.
